questions.text: The sum of 3 numbers is 1305. The first number is 360. The second number is twice the first number. What is the third number?
Mary had 129 apples. Tom had 127 more apples than Mary. Linda had 195 more apples than Tom. How many more apples did Linda have than Mary?
Jacob had twice as many marbles as Jerry. Kenny had 3 times as many marbles as Jacob. They had 846 marbles altogether. How many more marbles did Kenny have than Jerry?

There were 5 times as many strawberries as blueberries in a container. Joel ate half of the number of strawberries and 120 strawberries were left in the container. How many strawberries and blueberries were in the container at first?
315 children were going to the zoo. Each bus could seat 30 children. What was the least number of buses needed to take all the children to the zoo?
The sum of two numbers is 185. One number is 15 more than the other number. What are the two numbers?
A clock cost $24 and a watch cost $15 more than the clock. Jeffrey bought 2 clocks and 3 watches. How much money did he spend?
A buffet lunch cost $23.20 for an adult and $7.50 less for a child. Find the total amount of money that 4 adults and 5 children had to pay for the buffet lunch.
Alex and Bryan shared a cake at a party. Alex ate 1/3 of the cake while Bryan ate 1/9 of the cake. What fraction of the cake did they eat altogether?
Kate bought 1/2 kg of flour to bake a cake. After baking the cake, she had 1/8 kg of flour left. How much flour did Kate use?
Wendy ate 1/5 of a pizza and Amanda ate 1/2 of the same pizza. What fraction of the pizza was left?
George ate 1/4 of a cake and gave half of the remainder to Amy. What fraction of the cake was left?
David ran 1 km 250 m from his house to his school. After that, he cycled 2 km 960 m to the library. What was the total distance he had travelled? (Express your answer in metres.)
Alan bought 3 m 70 cm of string. He used 1 m 90 cm and cut the remaining length into 6 equal strips. He used 4 strips. What was the length of string left in the end?
Mrs Cole bought a cloth that was 3 m 50 cm long. She cut it into 5 equal pieces and used 3 such pieces. Find the length of cloth that she had left. (Express your answer in metres and centimetres.)
Mr Clement bought 16 sacks of soil. Each sack contained 9 kg of soil. He repacked the soil equally into bags, each weighing 3 kg. How many bags did he pack?
The mass of a container with a steel ball is 3800 g. When 3 more similar steel balls are added, the mass is 4700 g. What is the mass of the container?
Mr Watson is 7 times as old as his son this year. His son was 4 years old last year. How old will his son be when Mr Watson is 60 years old?
Sue is 3 times as old as Cassandra this year. Cassandra will be 20 years old next year. How old was Sue last year?
There were 480 apples and oranges in a box. The number of oranges was twice the number of apples in the box. (a) How many apples were there? (b) How many oranges were there?
The sum of two numbers is 780. One number is 245. What is the other number?
A school garden has 12 plots. Each plot has 18 tomato plants and 7 bean plants. How many plants are there altogether?
A farmer sold 2/5 of his 750 potatoes. How many potatoes did he have left?
A shop had 720 pencils. 1/6 were red, 1/4 were blue, and the rest were green. How many green pencils were there?
A rectangle has an area of 360 square metres and a width of 12 metres. What is its length?
